title: Quantization profile benchmark orchestration and regression SLA
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build an orchestrated benchmarking and load-testing harness that systematically evaluates quantization profiles (FP16, INT8, INT4) across representative workloads and detects quality vs performance regressions automatically. Deliverables: 1) standardized benchmark job spec that emits tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, memory footprint, and quality metrics (perplexity, BLEU/EM where applicable, and a set of task-specific acceptance tests), 2) load-scenario definitions (steady-state, ramp, spike, bursty prefixes) and traffic generator snippets, 3) regression detection rules and an alerting playbook tied to console dashboards and CI gating.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can run a full matrix (model-version x quant-profile x sequence-length x batch) and produce a CSV/JSON artifact with tokens_per_sec, p50_ms, p95_ms, 99_ms, gpu_mem_mb, and quality_score for each cell. 2) Regression engine flags >5% drop in tokens/sec or >10% increase in p95 for customer-facing profiles, and flags >2% BLEU/EM drop for quality-sensitive workloads. 3) CI integration: PRs that change quantization code trigger a smoke run and must not create a failing regression alert. 4) Results are viewable in console-qa dashboard and link back to the source job/commit.
implementation_notes:
- Reuse existing microbench harness from ENG-5824 for kernel timing but extend to sequence-length distributions from production traces.
- Use a representative prompt set (30k tokens across instruction/chat/long-form summarization/qa) stored in gdrive: link below.
- Quality measurement: add lightweight surrogate evals (LM perplexity on heldout, squad-like EM for QA, and a synthetic token accuracy for decoding-sensitive layers).
- Performance counters: capture tokens/sec per GPU, KV cache hit ratio, and batching stats. Store artifacts in s3://redwood-quantbench/YYYYMMDD/{job-id}.
- Regression detection: implement both absolute threshold rules and a rolling baseline comparator (7-day median) to filter noise.
- For INT4 runs, add a stability pass that repeats sample prompts 5x to detect nondeterministic degradation.
